slides.1.title: Pico's UNESCO Vineyards
slides.1.html:
The vineyards of Pico were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2004, because of their unique landscape of basalt stone walls (Currais).

🪨 The story of the basalt walls

  • Farmers used volcanic basalt to build countless small enclosures that protect the vines from strong Atlantic winds
  • These stone walls have existed for over 500 years
  • Seen from above they look like a giant black chessboard, a spectacular sight
  • Basalt is rich in minerals, giving the wines a distinctive salty minerality

🍾 Characteristics of Azores wine

  • Main varieties: Verdelho (white), Arinto dos Açores, Terrantez (white)
  • Style: fresh and high in acidity, with salty minerality and low alcohol (11-13%), well suited to seafood
  • Main IGP: Açores IGP (covering all the islands)
  • Pico, Graciosa and Terceira have DOC status
slides.2.question: What soil is the Pico vineyard on the Açores islands most famous for?
slides.2.explanation: Pico's vineyards are built on black basalt volcanic rock, and farmers protect the vines with walls of piled basalt. This landscape was recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004.

slides.3.description: Portugal's Atlantic island group, 1,500 km from the mainland; the basalt-walled vineyards of Pico are a UNESCO World Heritage Site
slides.4.title: The Three Açores DOCs: Supplement
slides.4.html:
The three Azorean islands with a DOC each have a different style:

  • Pico DOC: fortified whites, with alcohol after fortification required to be ≥ 16% and cask ageing ≥ 3 years; the varieties are Verdelho, Arinto and Terrantez, and the vineyards are sheltered by basalt stone walls
  • Biscoitos DOC (Terceira island): also fortified whites from the varieties above
  • Graciosa DOC: unfortified dry white table wines

Based on compiled data from 2011-2012.
